case_file.title: Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute
case_file.facts_summary: My name is Rohan Sen (rohan.sen@example.com, +91-9876543210), residing at 402 Palm Heights, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka. On 10th April 2024, I purchased an ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop from MegaKart India E-Commerce Pvt Ltd (Order ID: MK-202404-99210) for Rs. 89,999/- paid via ICICI Bank credit card. The seller on the marketplace was SuperDeals Retail India Pvt Ltd. The parcel arrived on 14th April 2024. Upon powering on the device, the screen started flickering uncontrollably with persistent horizontal green scanlines, and the dedicated GPU repeatedly crashed under standard workload. Within 24 hours of delivery, on 15th April 2024, I initiated a return request on MegaKart's platform. On 16th April 2024, MegaKart abruptly closed my return ticket without an inspection, stating that their platform policy excludes electronics from direct replacement and directing me to contact the brand service center under Section 79 of the IT Act. On 18th April 2024, I took the laptop to the authorized PredatorTech/ASUS service center in Bengaluru (Job Sheet No: BLR-SRV-2024-8812). The service center confirmed that the motherboard and display panel had manufacturing defects, but refused replacement or warranty repair, claiming the unit was sold as an unauthorized clearance item on MegaKart and therefore void of replacement support. Both the marketplace platform and the manufacturer are pointing fingers at each other, refusing a refund of my Rs. 89,999/-.

**TO**: Grievance Redressal Officer, Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)
**EMAIL**: grievance-officer@ecommerce-platform.in
**DATE**: 2026-11-07
**SUBJECT**: FORMAL ESCALATION: Grievance under Rule 4(5) of Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 - Order regarding Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute

Dear Grievance Officer,

I am writing to formally lodge a statutory consumer grievance pursuant to **Rule 4(4) and Rule 4(5) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** regarding a transaction conducted on your platform.

### 1. TRANSACTION DETAILS
- **Complainant / Buyer**: Rohan Sen (9876543210, rohan.sen@example.com)
- **Transaction / Order Date**: 2026-11-07
- **Item / Service Purchased**: Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute
- **Valuable Consideration Paid**: ₹89,999.00
- **Opposite Party Seller**: Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)
- **Opposite Party Marketplace**: Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)

### 2. FACTUAL SUMMARY OF GRIEVANCE
My name is Rohan Sen (rohan.sen@example.com, +91-9876543210), residing at 402 Palm Heights, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka. On 10th April 2024, I purchased an ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop from MegaKart India E-Commerce Pvt Ltd (Order ID: MK-202404-99210) for Rs. 89,999/- paid via ICICI Bank credit card. The seller on the marketplace was SuperDeals Retail India Pvt Ltd. The parcel arrived on 14th April 2024. Upon powering on the device, the screen started flickering uncontrollably with persistent horizontal green scanlines, and the dedicated GPU repeatedly crashed under standard workload. Within 24 hours of delivery, on 15th April 2024, I initiated a return request on MegaKart's platform. On 16th April 2024, MegaKart abruptly closed my return ticket without an inspection, stating that their platform policy excludes electronics from direct replacement and directing me to contact the brand service center under Section 79 of the IT Act. On 18th April 2024, I took the laptop to the authorized PredatorTech/ASUS service center in Bengaluru (Job Sheet No: BLR-SRV-2024-8812). The service center confirmed that the motherboard and display panel had manufacturing defects, but refused replacement or warranty repair, claiming the unit was sold as an unauthorized clearance item on MegaKart and therefore void of replacement support. Both the marketplace platform and the manufacturer are pointing fingers at each other, refusing a refund of my Rs. 89,999/-.

Despite bringing this matter to the attention of customer support, my legitimate request for refund / replacement was unlawfully denied.

### 3. STATUTORY BREACHES
1. **Rule 4(5)(b) & (c), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020**: Mandatory statutory obligation of the Grievance Officer to acknowledge receipt within forty-eight (48) hours with a ticket number, and redress within thirty (30) days.
2. **Rule 6(3) & Rule 7(4), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020**: Absolute prohibition against refusal to refund consideration paid or take back goods that are defective, deficient, or spurious.
3. **Section 2(11), Consumer Protection Act, 2019**: Gross deficiency in service by failing to deliver goods as represented and denying legitimate post-sale remedy.

### 4. FORMAL DEMANDS
Pursuant to the mandatory statutory framework, you are hereby called upon to:
1. **Acknowledge this grievance within forty-eight (48) hours** from receipt and issue an official Complaint Ticket Number.
2. **Initiate and credit a full refund of ₹89,999.00** to my original payment source within **seven (7) working days**.
3. **Provide full written resolution** within thirty (30) days as mandated under Rule 4(5)(c).

Please be advised that failure to resolve this complaint within the statutory window will constrain me to escalate this matter to the **National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915)**, register a formal complaint with the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** under Section 18 of CPA 2019, and institute legal proceedings before the competent Consumer Commission via **e-Daakhil (`edaakhil.nic.in`)**, claiming full refund with 18% interest, compensation for mental agony, and litigation expenses.

Yours faithfully,

**Rohan Sen**
Address on record
Email: rohan.sen@example.com | Phone: 9876543210

**(ISSUED UNDER SECTIONS 2(10), 2(11), 2(47), AND 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019 READ WITH RULES 4, 5, AND 6 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION (E-COMMERCE) RULES, 2020)**

**SENT VIA REGISTERED POST WITH ACKNOWLEDGMENT DUE (RPAD) & SPEED POST & REGISTERED EMAIL**

**Place**: Bengaluru, India

**FROM**:
**Rohan Sen** (Complainant / Consumer)

Email: rohan.sen@example.com | Phone: 9876543210

**SUBJECT**: FORMAL LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE: Under Section 35 CPA 2019 demanding refund of ₹89,999.00 with 18% interest and compensation regarding Order for Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute

---

SIRS / MADAM,

Under instructions and on behalf of myself, **Rohan Sen**, a bona fide consumer, I do hereby serve upon you this Formal Legal Notice:

### 1. BONA FIDE CONSUMER STATUS (SECTION 2(7) CPA 2019)
That the Complainant is a bona fide "consumer" within the meaning of **Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019**, having purchased goods/services for personal use for valuable consideration paid, and is not engaged in any commercial resale.

### 2. TRANSACTION AND FACTUAL MATRIX
1. That on **2026-11-07**, the Complainant ordered **Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute** from Opposite Party No. 1 through Opposite Party No. 2's platform, paying **₹89,999.00** electronically.
2. That upon delivery, the Complainant discovered:
My name is Rohan Sen (rohan.sen@example.com, +91-9876543210), residing at 402 Palm Heights, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka. On 10th April 2024, I purchased an ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop from MegaKart India E-Commerce Pvt Ltd (Order ID: MK-202404-99210) for Rs. 89,999/- paid via ICICI Bank credit card. The seller on the marketplace was SuperDeals Retail India Pvt Ltd. The parcel arrived on 14th April 2024. Upon powering on the device, the screen started flickering uncontrollably with persistent horizontal green scanlines, and the dedicated GPU repeatedly crashed under standard workload. Within 24 hours of delivery, on 15th April 2024, I initiated a return request on MegaKart's platform. On 16th April 2024, MegaKart abruptly closed my return ticket without an inspection, stating that their platform policy excludes electronics from direct replacement and directing me to contact the brand service center under Section 79 of the IT Act. On 18th April 2024, I took the laptop to the authorized PredatorTech/ASUS service center in Bengaluru (Job Sheet No: BLR-SRV-2024-8812). The service center confirmed that the motherboard and display panel had manufacturing defects, but refused replacement or warranty repair, claiming the unit was sold as an unauthorized clearance item on MegaKart and therefore void of replacement support. Both the marketplace platform and the manufacturer are pointing fingers at each other, refusing a refund of my Rs. 89,999/-.
3. That the Complainant reported the issue immediately, but Opposite Parties unlawfully denied return/refund citing arbitrary internal policies.

### 3. STATUTORY BREACHES AND UNLAWFUL CONDUCT
1. **Defect in Goods (Section 2(10), CPA 2019)**: The goods supplied suffer from material faults, substandard quality, and non-conformity with representations made.
2. **Gross Deficiency in Service (Section 2(11), CPA 2019)**: Opposite Parties failed to fulfill statutory post-sale duties and arbitrarily rejected return requests.
3. **Unfair Trade Practice (Section 2(47)(viii), CPA 2019)**: Unlawful refusal to take back defective goods and refund consideration paid.
4. **Violation of E-Commerce Rules, 2020**:
   - **Rule 6(3)**: Explicit statutory bar prohibiting sellers from refusing refunds.
   - **Rule 4(5)**: Mandatory grievance resolution timeline violated.
   - **Non-Exemption under IT Act Section 79**: Under Rule 5(1), marketplace entities cannot seek intermediary safe harbor exemption while actively facilitating unfair trade practices.

### 4. PEREMPTORY 15-DAY DEMAND
You are hereby jointly and severally called upon to comply with the following demands within **FIFTEEN (15) DAYS** from the date of receipt of this Legal Notice:
1. **Full Refund**: Immediately refund **₹89,999.00** along with interest at the rate of **18% per annum** from the date of payment until realization.
2. **Compensation**: Pay an amount of **₹25,000.00** towards mental agony, severe harassment, trauma, and loss of valuable time caused to the Complainant.
3. **Legal Expenses**: Pay a sum of **₹5,000.00** towards legal notice expenses.

### 5. NOTICE OF LEGAL ACTION (E-DAAKHIL FILING)
Please take notice that if you fail to comply with the aforesaid demands within the stipulated period of **15 days**, the Complainant shall institute an online consumer complaint before the competent **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** under **Section 35 of CPA 2019 via e-Daakhil (`edaakhil.nic.in`)**.

In that event, you shall be held jointly and severally liable for all consequential damages, punitive damages, and full costs of litigation at your sole risk and peril.

**Copy retained for official records and production before the Hon'ble Consumer Commission.**

Yours faithfully,

**Rohan Sen**
(Complainant / Party-in-Person)

# BEFORE THE HON'BLE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION AT BENGALURU, DELHI

**(INSTITUTED UNDER SECTION 35 READ WITH SECTION 34(2)(d) OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019)**

---

**VERSUS**

1. **Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)** (Seller)
   Registered Office: Address on file / Platform seller directory
   ... **OPPOSITE PARTY NO. 1**

### PART II: INDEX OF DOCUMENTS

| Sl. No. | Description of Annexure | Annexure Marker |
|:---:|:---|:---:|

| 4. | Photographic Proof / Video Recording of Defective / Spurious Goods | **Annexure C-3** |
| 5. | Email Communication & Customer Support Denial Records | **Annexure C-4** |
| 6. | Copy of Formal 15-Day Legal Demand Notice dated 2026-11-07 with Postal Receipt | **Annexure C-5** |

---

### PART III: STATEMENT OF MATERIAL FACTS

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. **Status of Parties**:
   The Complainant is an individual residing at Bengaluru, Delhi, and is a bona fide "consumer" under **Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019**. The goods/services were purchased solely for personal use for valuable consideration paid, and not for commercial resale. Opposite Party No. 1 is the registered seller, and Opposite Party No. 2 is the marketplace platform under the E-Commerce Rules, 2020.

2. **Purchase Transaction & Consideration**:
   On **2026-11-07**, the Complainant purchased **Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute** through Opposite Party No. 2's marketplace, paying valuable consideration of **₹89,999.00** (**Annexure C-1 and C-2**).

3. **Defect & Grievance**:
   My name is Rohan Sen (rohan.sen@example.com, +91-9876543210), residing at 402 Palm Heights, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka. On 10th April 2024, I purchased an ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop from MegaKart India E-Commerce Pvt Ltd (Order ID: MK-202404-99210) for Rs. 89,999/- paid via ICICI Bank credit card. The seller on the marketplace was SuperDeals Retail India Pvt Ltd. The parcel arrived on 14th April 2024. Upon powering on the device, the screen started flickering uncontrollably with persistent horizontal green scanlines, and the dedicated GPU repeatedly crashed under standard workload. Within 24 hours of delivery, on 15th April 2024, I initiated a return request on MegaKart's platform. On 16th April 2024, MegaKart abruptly closed my return ticket without an inspection, stating that their platform policy excludes electronics from direct replacement and directing me to contact the brand service center under Section 79 of the IT Act. On 18th April 2024, I took the laptop to the authorized PredatorTech/ASUS service center in Bengaluru (Job Sheet No: BLR-SRV-2024-8812). The service center confirmed that the motherboard and display panel had manufacturing defects, but refused replacement or warranty repair, claiming the unit was sold as an unauthorized clearance item on MegaKart and therefore void of replacement support. Both the marketplace platform and the manufacturer are pointing fingers at each other, refusing a refund of my Rs. 89,999/-.

4. **Arbitrary Denial & Statutory Breach**:
   The Complainant immediately reported the grievance to Opposite Parties. Opposite Parties arbitrarily refused return/refund, directly violating Rule 4(5) and Rule 6(3) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.

5. **Exhaustion of Pre-Litigation Notice**:
   The Complainant dispatched a formal 15-day Legal Demand Notice upon Opposite Parties on 2026-11-07 (**Annexure C-5**). Opposite Parties failed to remedy the grievance within the stipulated window.

---

### PART IV: STATUTORY GROUNDS OF CLAIM

The present complaint is instituted on the following distinct legal grounds:

- **GROUND A (GROSS DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE - SECTION 2(11) CPA 2019)**:
  Opposite Parties acted with gross deficiency, imperfection, and inadequacy in the quality and manner of performance required by law and contract.

- **GROUND B (DEFECT IN GOODS - SECTION 2(10) CPA 2019)**:
  The goods delivered were defective, substandard, and failed to conform to the representations.

- **GROUND C (UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE - SECTION 2(47)(viii) CPA 2019)**:
  Opposite Parties adopted an unfair trade practice by unlawfully refusing to take back defective goods and refund consideration paid within thirty days.

- **GROUND D (VIOLATION OF CONSUMER PROTECTION (E-COMMERCE) RULES, 2020)**:
  Opposite Party No. 1 violated Rule 6(3) barring refusal of refunds. Opposite Party No. 2 breached Rule 4(4) and Rule 4(5) by failing to ensure proper grievance officer redressal.

- **GROUND E (JOINT AND SEVERAL LIABILITY)**:
  Pursuant to Rule 5(1) of the E-Commerce Rules, Opposite Party No. 2 cannot claim safe harbor under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and is jointly and severally liable.

---

### PART V: PECUNIARY & TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION

1. **Pecuniary Jurisdiction**:
   The value of consideration paid is **₹89,999.00**, which does not exceed ₹50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs). Hence, this Hon'ble District Commission has competent pecuniary jurisdiction under **Rule 3 of the 2021 Pecuniary Rules**.

2. **Territorial Jurisdiction**:
   The Complainant resides and personally works for gain at **Bengaluru, Delhi**. Territorial jurisdiction is expressly conferred under **Section 34(2)(d) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019**.

3. **Statutory Filing Fee**:
   The statutory filing fee is **₹0** under the statutory schedule, payable online via Bharatkosh on e-Daakhil (Nil fee for consideration up to ₹5,00,000/-).

---

### PART VI: LIMITATION STATEMENT (SECTION 69)

The cause of action first arose on **2026-11-07** when Opposite Parties rejected the return/refund. The present complaint is instituted within the mandatory 2-year limitation period (730 days) prescribed under **Section 69(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019**.

---

### PART VII: PRAYER / RELIEF SOUGHT

WHEREFORE, in light of the above facts, grounds, and statutory provisions, the Complainant most respectfully prays that this Hon'ble Commission may be pleased to:

a) **Direct Opposite Parties jointly and severally to refund** the full consideration amount of **₹89,999.00** along with interest @ **12% per annum** from the date of payment until realization;
b) **Award compensation of ₹25,000.00** against Opposite Parties for mental harassment, trauma, agony, and hardship caused to the Complainant;
c) **Award litigation costs of ₹5,000.00** incurred in pursuing these proceedings; and
d) **Pass such other and further relief(s)** as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice.

**COMPLAINANT**
Through: Self (Party-in-Person)
Place: Bengaluru
Date: 2026-11-07

---

Dear Grievance Officer,

I am writing to formally lodge a statutory consumer grievance pursuant to **Rule 4(4) and Rule 4(5) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** regarding a transaction conducted on your platform.

### 1. TRANSACTION DETAILS
- **Complainant / Buyer**: Rohan Sen (9876543210, rohan.sen@example.com)
- **Transaction / Order Date**: 2026-11-07
- **Item / Service Purchased**: Defective Laptop Refund Refusal Dispute
- **Valuable Consideration Paid**: ₹89,999.00
- **Opposite Party Seller**: Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)
- **Opposite Party Marketplace**: Opposite Party (Merchant / Platform)

### 2. FACTUAL SUMMARY OF GRIEVANCE
My name is Rohan Sen (rohan.sen@example.com, +91-9876543210), residing at 402 Palm Heights, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka. On 10th April 2024, I purchased an ASUS ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop from MegaKart India E-Commerce Pvt Ltd (Order ID: MK-202404-99210) for Rs. 89,999/- paid via ICICI Bank credit card. The seller on the marketplace was SuperDeals Retail India Pvt Ltd. The parcel arrived on 14th April 2024. Upon powering on the device, the screen started flickering uncontrollably with persistent horizontal green scanlines, and the dedicated GPU repeatedly crashed under standard workload. Within 24 hours of delivery, on 15th April 2024, I initiated a return request on MegaKart's platform. On 16th April 2024, MegaKart abruptly closed my return ticket without an inspection, stating that their platform policy excludes electronics from direct replacement and directing me to contact the brand service center under Section 79 of the IT Act. On 18th April 2024, I took the laptop to the authorized PredatorTech/ASUS service center in Bengaluru (Job Sheet No: BLR-SRV-2024-8812). The service center confirmed that the motherboard and display panel had manufacturing defects, but refused replacement or warranty repair, claiming the unit was sold as an unauthorized clearance item on MegaKart and therefore void of replacement support. Both the marketplace platform and the manufacturer are pointing fingers at each other, refusing a refund of my Rs. 89,999/-.

Despite bringing this matter to the attention of customer support, my legitimate request for refund / replacement was unlawfully denied.

### 3. STATUTORY BREACHES
1. **Rule 4(5)(b) & (c), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020**: Mandatory statutory obligation of the Grievance Officer to acknowledge receipt within forty-eight (48) hours with a ticket number, and redress within thirty (30) days.
2. **Rule 6(3) & Rule 7(4), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020**: Absolute prohibition against refusal to refund consideration paid or take back goods that are defective, deficient, or spurious.
3. **Section 2(11), Consumer Protection Act, 2019**: Gross deficiency in service by failing to deliver goods as represented and denying legitimate post-sale remedy.

### 4. FORMAL DEMANDS
Pursuant to the mandatory statutory framework, you are hereby called upon to:
1. **Acknowledge this grievance within forty-eight (48) hours** from receipt and issue an official Complaint Ticket Number.
2. **Initiate and credit a full refund of ₹89,999.00** to my original payment source within **seven (7) working days**.
3. **Provide full written resolution** within thirty (30) days as mandated under Rule 4(5)(c).

Please be advised that failure to resolve this complaint within the statutory window will constrain me to escalate this matter to the **National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915)**, register a formal complaint with the **Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)** under Section 18 of CPA 2019, and institute legal proceedings before the competent Consumer Commission via **e-Daakhil (`edaakhil.nic.in`)**, claiming full refund with 18% interest, compensation for mental agony, and litigation expenses.

Yours faithfully,

**Rohan Sen**
Address on record
Email: rohan.sen@example.com | Phone: 9876543210

flaws_in_merchant_defense: Privity of contract exists between the consumer and the seller/platform from whom consideration was paid (Section 2(7)). The consumer has no privity with the seller's logistics contractor.
Under Section 2(11) of CPA 2019, transit failure or courier mishandling engaged by the merchant constitutes 'deficiency in service' directly attributable to the merchant.

suggested_counter_arguments: The consumer paid consideration to the platform/seller, establishing privity of contract under Section 2(7); logistics partners are agents of the seller.
Failure to deliver goods intact constitutes deficiency in service under Section 2(11) of CPA 2019, for which the merchant bears vicarious and direct liability.
Under Rule 6(3) of E-Commerce Rules 2020, sellers cannot refuse returns or refunds by deflecting consumers to third-party manufacturers.
